editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The stage descriptions, the TrivialLayout/VF2Layout/SabreLayout conditions, the claim that the NP-hard SWAP mapping is "prohibitively expensive" (계산 비용이 엄청나게 높습니다), and the Toffoli "up to six CNOT" cost all match the English. A few spots read as translationese. [30] calques the English nominal subject ("확률적 방법의 사용은 … 보장하지 않음을 의미합니다"). [59] softens "will likely change" to "변경될 수 있습니다". The Scheduling heading [63] is translated as "스케줄링", while every other stage heading keeps the English name (Init/Layout/Routing/Translation/Optimization 단계).

examples.source: The use of a stochastic method means that the circuits generated are not guaranteed to be the same over repeated runs.
examples.translation: 확률적 방법의 사용은 반복 실행에서 생성된 Circuit이 동일하다는 것을 보장하지 않음을 의미합니다.
examples.suggested: 확률적 방법을 쓰기 때문에 실행할 때마다 같은 Circuit이 생성된다는 보장은 없어요.
examples.why: Calqued English nominal-subject structure. A Korean technical writer would put it as a cause and its result.

examples.source: Therefore, the numbers below will likely change each time you run the code.
examples.translation: 따라서 아래 숫자는 코드를 실행할 때마다 변경될 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 따라서 아래 숫자는 코드를 실행할 때마다 달라질 가능성이 높습니다.
examples.why: 'will likely' (probably will) is softened to 'may'. The claim gets weaker, though not enough to mislead.
Every other stage heading keeps the English stage name plus 단계. This one switches convention.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural 해요체 throughout, with the core terms correct and glossed on first use (밀도 행렬(density matrices), 채널(channels), 측정(measurements), 조작적(operational)), and the Credly data-sharing caveat in [17] is kept in full.

The meaning holds throughout. The variational upper-bound caveat [178], the pole and equator distribution [144], the negative reaction energy [204] and the true/false items [216]-[220] all match the English, and nothing is invented. The problems are consistency only. "Trial wave function" is 시험 파동 함수 in [24]/[133] but 시도 파동 함수 in [30]-[33]. "Ansatz" moves between 앤사츠, Ansatz and ansatz ([93], [175], [253]-[268]). The Qiskit-patterns step headings switch from 1단계 [127] to "Step 2/3/4" [150]-[179]. The word bank translates only 바닥 상태 에너지 [102] and leaves the other terms and the answer key in English. Smaller slips: qubit reduction is both 축소 [87] and 감소 [128]/[172], and "(Optional)" in [253] is untranslated.

examples.why: [24] and [133] render 'trial function' as 시험 함수; the exercise switches to 시도, so the learner sees two names for the same object.
[118]-[121] and [127] use 1단계/2단계, but later headings ([150], [154], [159], [171]-[179]) keep the English 'Step N'. Target is also both 목표 and 대상.

examples.suggested: Translate all word-bank items and answers consistently (e.g. 고전 최적화기, 분자 해밀토니안, 양자 컴퓨팅), or keep all of them in English
examples.why: Only one word-bank item is translated. The others ([101], [105], [107]) and the answer key ([109]-[113]) stay English, which is inconsistent for a fill-in exercise written in Korean.

examples.source: (Optional) Appendix: Optimizer overhead by ansatz complexity
examples.translation: (Optional) 부록: Ansatz 복잡도에 따른 최적화기 오버헤드
examples.suggested: (선택) 부록: 앤사츠 복잡도에 따른 최적화기 오버헤드
examples.why: '(Optional)' is left untranslated, and the appendix uses 'Ansatz' while the main body uses 앤사츠.

examples.translation: 해밀토니안의 패리티(parity)를 이용한 qubit 감소를 수행하여
examples.suggested: 해밀토니안의 패리티를 이용한 qubit 축소를 수행하여
examples.why: [87] calls the same technique qubit 축소; [128] and [172] switch to 감소.
